newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks bullish after new economic steps.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks bullish after new economic steps.

text.p: Jordanian stocks ended sharply higher on Monday with buoyed investor confidence after the government announced steps to boost the private sector in the wake of bread riots, dealers said.

The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 1.46 percent to 141.31 points from 139.27 points on Sunday, rising above the key 140-point psychological barrier for the first time since the riots broke out a week ago.
The market first fell below 140 points at the end of June, sliding to levels not reached since 1993, with lack of liquidity and minimal institutional support.

"This uptick is somewhat an immediate reaction and without tangible translation of these reforms this upward trend will peter out," said Omar al-Masri, managing director of Atlas Invesment Group, a firm involved with foriegn funds.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- firmed 0.79 percent to 80.44 points. It was 15.78 percent down on last year.

Monday's rise represented an increase of almost two percent in the index over the last week, as the market recovered from unrest fuelled by the government's decision this month to almost double prices of bread in line with IMF-agreed economic reforms.
The riots were the worst in Jordan since 1989.
In banks, the leading sector: blue-chip Arab Bank rose 7.250 dinars to 228.50 dinars while Jordan Kuwait Bank rose 10 fils to 2.690 fils on a turnover of 275,992 dinars.
In industrials, the leading sector, Jordan Cement Factories rose 50 fils to 3.340 dinars and Livestock and Poultry firmed 30 fils to 530 fils.

In services, Jordan Electric Power rose 10 fils to 1.540 dinars and National Portfolio rose 60 fils to 1.180 dinars. Banks dominated on Monday, with a 577,705 dinar turnover and the index rose 2.45 percent. Industrials posted turnover of 204,935 dinars and the index rose 0.43 percent, while services posted a low 21,958 dinar turnover and the index rose 0.35 percent.
A total of 131,365 shares worth 80,389 dinars changed hands in weak trade on the parallel market.
